items.name: Establishment of religion restriction
items.summary: Congress may make no law respecting an establishment of religion.

items.name: Free exercise of religion
items.summary: Congress may not prohibit free exercise of religion.

items.name: Freedom of speech
items.summary: Congress may not abridge freedom of speech.

items.name: Freedom of press
items.summary: Congress may not abridge freedom of the press.

items.name: Peaceable assembly
items.summary: The people retain constitutional protection to peaceably assemble.

items.name: Petition government for redress
items.summary: The people retain protection to petition the government for redress of grievances.

items.name: Well-regulated militia prefatory language
items.summary: The text references a well-regulated militia as necessary to the security of a free State; doctrinal implications are separate.

items.name: Right to keep and bear arms
items.summary: The constitutional right of the people to keep and bear arms shall not be infringed, subject to controlling doctrine.

items.name: Quartering soldiers in peacetime
items.summary: No soldier may be quartered in any house during peacetime without the owner's consent.

items.name: Quartering soldiers in wartime
items.summary: During war, quartering must be in a manner prescribed by law.

items.name: Security against unreasonable searches and seizures
items.summary: The people have a right to be secure in persons, houses, papers and effects against unreasonable searches and seizures.

items.name: Warrant probable cause and sworn support
items.summary: A warrant cannot issue without probable cause supported by oath or affirmation.

items.name: Warrant particularity
items.summary: Warrants must particularly describe the place to be searched and persons or things to be seized.

items.name: Grand jury indictment or presentment
items.summary: A person shall not be held to answer for a capital or otherwise infamous crime without grand jury presentment or indictment, subject to textual exceptions.

items.name: Grand jury land/naval and militia exception
items.summary: Text excepts cases arising in land or naval forces, or the militia when in actual service in time of war or public danger.

items.name: Double jeopardy safeguard
items.summary: No person may be twice put in jeopardy of life or limb for the same offense.

items.name: Self-incrimination safeguard
items.summary: No person in any criminal case shall be compelled to be a witness against themself.

items.name: Federal due process
items.summary: No person may be deprived of life, liberty or property without due process of law by the federal government.

items.name: Public-use taking
items.summary: Private property may be taken for public use only subject to the Just Compensation Clause.

items.name: Just compensation for public takings
items.summary: Private property taken for public use requires just compensation.

items.name: Speedy criminal trial
items.summary: Accused persons have the right to a speedy trial in covered criminal prosecutions.

items.name: Public criminal trial
items.summary: Accused persons have the right to a public trial in covered criminal prosecutions.

items.name: Impartial jury and proper district
items.summary: Covered prosecutions require an impartial jury of the State and district where crime committed; district previously ascertained by law.

items.name: Notice of nature and cause of accusation
items.summary: The accused must be informed of the nature and cause of the accusation.

items.name: Confrontation of adverse witnesses
items.summary: The accused has the right to be confronted with the witnesses against them.

items.name: Compulsory process for witnesses
items.summary: The accused may have compulsory process for obtaining witnesses in their favor.

items.name: Assistance of counsel
items.summary: The accused has the right to assistance of counsel for their defense.

items.name: Jury trial in federal civil suits at common law
items.summary: In suits at common law where value in controversy exceeds twenty dollars, the jury-trial right is preserved.

items.name: Jury-found facts re-examination restriction
items.summary: No fact tried by jury may be otherwise re-examined in a U.S. court than under rules of common law.

items.name: Excessive bail
items.summary: Excessive bail shall not be required.

items.name: Excessive fines
items.summary: Excessive fines shall not be imposed.

items.name: Cruel and unusual punishments
items.summary: Cruel and unusual punishments shall not be inflicted.

items.name: Unenumerated rights retained by people
items.summary: Constitutional enumeration of certain rights shall not be construed to deny or disparage others retained by the people.

items.name: Powers reserved to States
items.summary: Powers not delegated to United States nor prohibited to States are reserved to States respectively.

items.name: Powers reserved to the people
items.summary: The same undelegated and nonprohibited powers are alternatively reserved to the people.

items.name: Federal court suit restriction against States
items.summary: Judicial power cannot be construed to extend to specified suits in law or equity against a State.

items.name: Interstate and foreign claimant restriction
items.summary: The express Eleventh Amendment rule concerns suits against a State commenced or prosecuted by citizens of another State or foreign citizens/subjects.

items.name: Separate ballots for President and Vice President
items.summary: Presidential electors cast distinct ballots for President and Vice President and list each category separately.

items.name: Presidential and Vice Presidential inhabitation restriction
items.summary: At least one candidate voted for must not be an inhabitant of the elector's State.

items.name: Elector lists certified and transmitted
items.summary: Electors make, sign, certify and transmit lists of votes to the President of the Senate.

items.name: Congressional counting process
items.summary: The President of the Senate opens certificates in the presence of both Houses, and votes are counted subject to enacted law.

items.name: Presidential Electoral College majority
items.summary: The highest presidential vote recipient is elected President if majority of electors appointed.

items.name: House contingent presidential election
items.summary: Without a majority the House chooses President from no more than top three presidential electoral candidates; State delegations vote by State with special quorum and majority requirements.

items.name: Senate contingent vice presidential election
items.summary: Without majority for Vice President, Senate chooses from top two with two-thirds quorum and majority-of-whole-Senate requirement.

items.name: Vice Presidential eligibility tied to Presidency
items.summary: A person constitutionally ineligible to office of President is ineligible to be Vice President.

items.name: Abolition of slavery and involuntary servitude
items.summary: Slavery and involuntary servitude shall not exist in United States or any place subject to their jurisdiction, except for the specified conviction-based punishment clause.

items.name: Crime-conviction punishment exception
items.summary: The narrow original exception is punishment for crime whereof a party shall have been duly convicted; it is not a general license for slavery.

items.name: Congressional Thirteenth Amendment enforcement
items.summary: Congress may enforce the Thirteenth Amendment by appropriate legislation.

items.name: Birth/naturalization and U.S. citizenship
items.summary: Persons born or naturalized in United States and subject to its jurisdiction are citizens of United States.

items.name: State citizenship by State residence
items.summary: Qualified U.S. citizens are citizens of the State where they reside.

items.name: Privileges or immunities of national citizenship
items.summary: No State shall make or enforce law abridging privileges or immunities of U.S. citizens.

items.name: Due process against States for persons
items.summary: No State shall deprive any person of life, liberty or property without due process.

items.name: Equal protection against States for persons
items.summary: No State may deny any person within its jurisdiction equal protection of the laws.

items.name: Representative apportionment by persons
items.summary: Representatives shall be apportioned among States according to their respective numbers, with text and subsequent changes.

items.name: Historical original exclusion category
items.summary: Original text referred to excluding 'Indians not taxed'; preserve as historical text only, not a present rule authorizing race-based exclusion.

items.name: Representation reduction for vote denial or abridgment
items.summary: Section 2 describes reduction of State representation for abridged/denied specified voting rights with textual exceptions and later constitutional changes.

items.name: Original voting-age and male-voter reference
items.summary: Historical 21-year-old male citizen reference is modified by subsequent suffrage amendments including XXVI; do not treat as a modern eligibility limit.

items.name: Participation in rebellion or other crime exception
items.summary: The original apportionment vote-denial formula excepts participation in rebellion or other crime; scope requires jurisprudence.

items.name: Prior qualifying constitutional oath
items.summary: Section 3 disqualification is tethered to a previously described oath to support Constitution and specified classes of officials.

items.name: Insurrection/rebellion and aid-and-comfort criterion
items.summary: Section 3 specifies engaging in insurrection or rebellion or giving aid or comfort to enemies, under constitutional office criteria.

items.name: Covered federal and State constitutional offices
items.summary: Coverage includes named federal and State offices with specified oaths and prerequisites; application contested doctrine handled separately.

items.name: Congress can remove disability by two-thirds each House
items.summary: Congress may remove Section 3 disability by a vote of two-thirds of each House.

items.name: Validity of authorized federal public debt
items.summary: Validity of public debt of United States, authorized by law, including enumerated suppression of insurrection/rebellion debts, shall not be questioned.

items.name: No assumption/payment of rebellion debt
items.summary: Neither United States nor any State may assume or pay debt incurred in aid of insurrection or rebellion against United States.

items.name: No compensation for loss/emancipation of enslaved people
items.summary: Neither United States nor any State may assume or pay claims for loss or emancipation of enslaved persons; such claims are illegal and void.

items.name: Congressional enforcement of Fourteenth Amendment
items.summary: Congress shall have power to enforce Fourteenth Amendment provisions by appropriate legislation.

items.name: Voting rights irrespective of race
items.summary: Right of U.S. citizens to vote shall not be denied or abridged by United States or any State on account of race.

items.name: Voting rights irrespective of color
items.summary: Citizens' voting rights shall not be denied or abridged on account of color.

items.name: Voting rights irrespective of prior condition of servitude
items.summary: Citizens' voting rights shall not be denied or abridged on account of previous condition of servitude.

items.name: Congressional Fifteenth Amendment enforcement
items.summary: Congress may enforce Fifteenth Amendment by appropriate legislation.

items.name: Congressional taxation of incomes
items.summary: Congress has power to lay and collect taxes on incomes from whatever source derived, subject to constitutional limits.

items.name: Income-tax apportionment exception
items.summary: Income taxes described by Sixteenth Amendment may be laid without apportionment among States and without regard to any census or enumeration.

items.name: Direct election of two Senators per State
items.summary: The people of each State elect two Senators for six-year terms, each with one vote.

items.name: Senate elector qualifications from most numerous State legislative chamber
items.summary: Electors in each State have qualifications requisite for electors of most numerous branch of State legislature, subject to later amendments and voting rights law.

items.name: State executive issues Senate vacancy election writ
items.summary: When Senate vacancy occurs, State executive authority issues writs of election to fill vacancy.

items.name: State legislature may enable temporary Senate appointments
items.summary: State legislature may empower executive to make temporary Senate appointments until voters fill vacancy by election.

items.name: Senate membership prior to ratification protected
items.summary: Original transition rule protects election or term of any Senator chosen before Amendment XVII became valid; historical transitional exception.

items.name: Historical national prohibition of beverage alcohol
items.summary: Repealed national ban on manufacture, sale and transport of intoxicating liquors for beverage purposes; not current constitutional authority.

items.name: Historical delayed one-year prohibition effect
items.summary: Repealed amendment's substantive prohibition was deferred for one year from ratification before commencing January 1920.

items.name: Historical concurrent federal and State enforcement
items.summary: Repealed Article XVIII allocated concurrent enforcement authority to Congress and States; this authority ended with repeal in 1933.

items.name: Historical seven-year State legislative ratification deadline
items.summary: Repealed amendment's ratification prerequisite had to be satisfied within seven years and was met in 1919; not a recurring contemporary duty.

items.name: Voting rights not denied on account of sex
items.summary: Voting rights of U.S. citizens may not be denied or abridged by United States or States on account of sex.

items.name: Congressional Nineteenth Amendment enforcement
items.summary: Congress may enforce Nineteenth Amendment by appropriate legislation.

items.name: Presidential and vice presidential term start and end January 20
items.summary: President and Vice President terms end at noon January 20 in relevant years; successors' terms begin then.

items.name: Congressional term start and end January 3
items.summary: Senator and Representative terms end at noon January 3 in relevant years; successors' terms begin then.

items.name: Congress convenes annually January 3
items.summary: Congress must meet at least once annually beginning noon January 3 unless Congress by law appoints a different day.

items.name: Congress may set alternative annual meeting date by law
items.summary: Congress may by law appoint a different annual meeting day.

items.name: President-elect death: Vice-President-elect becomes President
items.summary: At beginning of term, if President-elect died, Vice-President-elect becomes President.

items.name: Failure to choose or qualify President: acting Vice President-elect
items.summary: If no President chosen before term or President-elect fails qualification, Vice-President-elect acts as President until President qualifies.

items.name: Congress may legislate when both incoming officers unqualified
items.summary: Congress may by law determine who acts as President if neither a President-elect nor a Vice-President-elect qualifies, subject to text.

items.name: Acting President limited until a successor qualifies
items.summary: Contingent acting President serves only until a President or Vice President qualifies, according to the relevant section.

items.name: House contingent presidential candidate death legislation
items.summary: Congress may by law address death of a person from whom House may choose a President in a contingent election.

items.name: Senate contingent vice presidential candidate death legislation
items.summary: Congress may by law address death of a person from whom Senate may choose a Vice President in a contingent election.

items.name: Historical effective date October 15 for Sections 1 and 2
items.summary: Sections 1 and 2 expressly entered legal effect October 15, 1933, rather than the January 1933 ratification date.

items.name: Historical seven-year ratification deadline
items.summary: Amendment XX required ratification by State legislatures within seven years of proposal; requirement fulfilled in 1933.

items.name: Constitutional repeal of Eighteenth Amendment
items.summary: Twenty-First Amendment Section 1 repealed Amendment XVIII as of ratification December 5, 1933.

items.name: Import and delivery contrary to State alcohol laws prohibited
items.summary: Transport/import of intoxicating liquor into a State, Territory or possession for delivery/use in violation of local law is prohibited, subject to controlling constitutional doctrine.

items.name: Historical convention ratification prerequisite within seven years
items.summary: Twenty-First Amendment used State conventions and a seven-year ratification window; condition fulfilled December 1933.

items.name: Two-election presidential limit
items.summary: No person may be elected President more than twice under Twenty-Second Amendment.

items.name: Service over two years of another elected term
items.summary: A person holding/acting as President for more than two years of another President's term may be elected President no more than once.

items.name: Historical incumbent and then-current-term exceptions
items.summary: Section 1's historically specific exemptions for officeholder at proposal and within the term at adoption do not create an unlimited modern exception.

items.name: Historical seven-year ratification limit
items.summary: Amendment XXII's seven-year legislative ratification requirement was met in February 1951.

items.name: District of Columbia selection of presidential electors
items.summary: District constituting seat of government appoints presidential electors as Congress may direct; DC does not thereby become a State.

items.name: District presidential electors capped by least populous State
items.summary: District receives electors equivalent to putative Senators and Representatives, but no more than least populous State.

items.name: District electors perform Twelfth Amendment duties
items.summary: District electors are additional to State electors and follow Twelfth Amendment presidential/vice presidential election mechanism.

items.name: Congressional Twenty-Third Amendment enforcement
items.summary: Congress may enforce Twenty-Third Amendment by appropriate legislation.

items.name: Federal election and primary poll-tax prohibition
items.summary: Citizens' federal election voting rights cannot be denied or abridged by federal/State governments for failure to pay a poll tax or other tax.

items.name: Enumerated federal offices and electors scope
items.summary: Twenty-Fourth Amendment text covers Presidential/VP elections and electors plus U.S. Senate and House elections, including primaries.

items.name: Congressional Twenty-Fourth Amendment enforcement
items.summary: Congress may enforce Twenty-Fourth Amendment by appropriate legislation.

items.name: Vice President succeeds permanently after presidential vacancy
items.summary: Upon presidential removal, death or resignation, Vice President becomes President; separate from Acting President on inability.

items.name: President nominates new Vice President for vacancy
items.summary: If Vice Presidency vacant, President nominates a new Vice President.

items.name: Both Houses must confirm new Vice President by majority
items.summary: Vice presidential nominee assumes office upon a majority vote of each House, not Senate-only advice and consent.

items.name: Written presidential declaration of inability
items.summary: President transmits written declaration of inability to President pro tempore Senate and Speaker House.

items.name: Vice President exercises powers as Acting President
items.summary: Upon declaration, Vice President discharges powers and duties as Acting President.

items.name: Presidential contrary declaration ends voluntary inability
items.summary: President may transmit contrary written declaration to resume powers under Section 3.

items.name: Vice President and majority officer/body inability declaration
items.summary: Vice President and majority principal executive officers (or substitute body Congress may by law provide) submit written inability declaration.

items.name: Vice President immediately becomes Acting President after declaration
items.summary: Following the written initial Section 4 inability declaration, Vice President immediately assumes powers as Acting President.

items.name: Presidential declaration of ability and four-day challenge window
items.summary: President may declare no inability exists; Vice President with specified majority may challenge by written declaration within four days.

items.name: Congress convenes within 48 hours if not in session
items.summary: Following the specified contested declaration, Congress must assemble within 48 hours if not in session.

items.name: Congressional 21-day decision period
items.summary: Congress must decide disputed inability within 21 days after receiving the latter declaration or after required assembly when not in session.

items.name: Two-thirds of both Houses for contested inability determination
items.summary: Continued Vice President Acting Presidency upon contested presidential ability requires a two-thirds vote of each House.

items.name: President resumes absent required dual supermajority
items.summary: If Congress does not meet the required constitutional two-thirds determination, President resumes powers and duties.

items.name: Voting protections for citizens 18 years or older
items.summary: Citizens of United States who are eighteen years of age or older have voting-right protection against age-based denial.

items.name: Federal and State age-based vote abridgment prohibition
items.summary: Neither United States nor any State may abridge covered citizens' voting rights on account of age.

items.name: Congressional Twenty-Sixth Amendment enforcement
items.summary: Congress may enforce Twenty-Sixth Amendment by appropriate legislation.

items.name: Intervening House election before congressional compensation variation
items.summary: A law varying Senators' or Representatives' compensation cannot take effect until an election of Representatives intervenes.
